title: Line Data from a Point and a Slope
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A line crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,3)$ and falls at a constant rate of $2$ units per unit of $x$. Write its equation and locate where the line meets the $x$-axis.

steps.title: Assemble the Slope-Intercept Form
steps.explanation: The point $(0,3)$ makes the $y$-intercept $b=3$, and the falling rate gives slope $m=-2$.
steps.why: Slope-intercept form reads directly off the given geometric data.

steps.title: Write the Equation
steps.explanation: Combining the parameters yields the linear model $y=-2x+3$.
steps.why: Every unit step right drops the line by two units.

steps.title: Solve for the x-Intercept
steps.explanation: Setting $y=0$ and solving gives $x=3/2$, so the line crosses the horizontal axis at $(3/2,0)$.
steps.why: On the $x$-axis the output must vanish, which converts the problem to solving a linear equation.
